labels.name: type:enhancement

labels.name: status:likely

body:
Thanks for implementing the file_uploader widget, I was really looking forward for that.

### Problem

My issue is that I expect large files (up to GBs), and thus reading them directly into memory is not acceptable for me. 

### Solution

**separate file_picker** One option would be to implement it as a separate widget (e.g. file_picker), which would just help to locate the file without uploading it.

**optional upload** Other possibility that comes to my mind would be an option (e.g. upload=False), that would allow me to choose not to upload the file. String with absolute path would be returned instead.

Also as mentioned in other issues, even if I could work with the file itself, I'd still need it's path, name, suffix etc. to work with.

**URL** Maybe in the future, but it would be really nice if the widget could also accept an URL.

Thanks in advance for considering the changes.

title: 2nd Sidebar (on right side)

labels.name: type:enhancement
labels.description: Requests for feature enhancements or new features

labels.name: area:layout
labels.description: Related to layout and positioning

body:
### Problem

A neat app often elucidates complex problems. Hence there is often a lot to explain to carry details about the app itself, its backgrounds and further details - especially for public apps. Currently, the little space in the sidebar and main window quickly get filled with explanations and further links. I have written long markdown documents one can hide, but still, either people quickly uncheck the box to head for the box or get overwhelmed with details. Eventually, a good app is not used because of a cluttered layout, long scrolling and still insufficient clarity.

### Solution

**MVP:** A 2nd sidebar on the right side could be a nice designated place for such instructions, background information etc. It would save a lot of real estate in the other sections and still provide novice users with guidance without distracting frequent users. Moreover I consider it rather simple to copy the class from the existing sidebar - just as a right-bound counterpart.

**Possible additions:** Another option cold be an annotation overlay for all controls.

**Preferred solution:** I prefer the simple and straight forward solution

### Additional context

Thanks so much and many cheers.
Conrad

title: Make Streamlit easy to deploy as a standalone executable (e.g. PyInstaller, Electron)

labels.name: type:enhancement
labels.description: Requests for feature enhancements or new features

labels.name: area:deployment
labels.description: Related to deployment of Streamlit apps

labels.name: status:unlikely
labels.description: Will probably not implement but looking for feedback

body:
Is there a future for electron deployment of streamlit?
___

```
streamlit electron app.py
```

Streamlits target demographic (seemingly the Data Science / ML / AI community) often has apps which consume *a lot* of resources. RAM for loading data used by the app can be quite a bit- pair this with `st.cache` and in a few hours/days time your streamlit app needs to be killed / controlled / scaled. That is fine (and good for AWS' profit), but why not be able to distribute the app across its users so they can run it on their machine (and use their resources).  This is easy enough if your streamlit users are capable of running `streamlit run ..` in their terminal. However, *who are the users of these apps*? Oftentimes they will be other engineers / programmers sure - but I think a substantial chunk of the user-base of streamlit apps is a non-technical audience. We send links to streamlit apps to management / non-technical members of the organization *constantly* I would much rather send them an `S3` link to download an electron app and not worry about scaling up the AWS instance(s) hosting it. Sure, they have to have python and some dependencies - but those are relatively easy to control by IT and can often involve little user work. Furthermore, we could maybe have a future where the `streamlit build electon` command could bundle dependencies? I am not sure - but it seems possible.


Streamlit seems well-positioned for this to be possible. It is trivial to "fake it". Just do something like this to get an *MVP*. 

```python
import streamlit as lit  # you guys really dropped the ball on this not being the suggested import
# idk - maybe it is too z00mer.

def main():
    lit.sidebar.title("Electron")
    lit.sidebar.info("The Electron Slide...")
    lit.sidebar.slider('How "nativive"?', 0, 100, 50)
    lit.title("Streamlit in `Electron`")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

Run it,

```
streamlit run app.py
```

Take the starter electron app from [here](https://github.com/electron/electron-quick-start). and change literally 1 line (:16)

```
mainWindow.loadURL('http://localhost:8501/')  // or wherever you served
```

And...

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8339189/79810221-8cb46680-8340-11ea-80a4-8d112f3b4611.png)

___
I am just opening this issue to see if you guys (and the community) think this has any legs. I am not sure of the specifics. For example,

```
streamlit (electron|run_electron) app.py  # for local testing and development
streamlit build -t electron app.py <name>  # for building and bundling dependencies
# to a downloadable launcher? 
...
```

Could there be electron-specific component implementations (so sidebar could be a native window), or tab support, keyboard shortcuts, etc? Could session state be saved to disk and loaded on app start to preserve state? Or maybe this is all a terrible idea... (also if there is another discussion of this already somewhere else (I couldn't find one) lmk and this can just be closed)

body:
### Summary

In my Streamlit app deployed in a standalone Docker container, local files can be uploaded via **st.file_uploader** without any problems. However, for the same app deployed on Kubernetes cluster in multiple replicas setting, st.file_uploader randomly returns HTTP status code 400 with an error message like: 

_**400: Invalid session_id: '1d319bd4-b1dc-4149-bfb2-24cdd48f3982'**_

![obraz](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7476899/145990286-42a04de9-298a-40ff-a2a7-fd6e9f31fac2.png)

The behaviour is non-deterministic - reloading (sometimes more than once) the browser tab helps.

### Steps to reproduce

- Deploy a Streamlit app on Kubernetes with multiple replicas
- Run the app in a browser
- Select any file in st.file_uploader's window.
- If the error doesn't occur, reload the browser tab and try again.

Code snippet:

```
st.file_uploader("Choose a file")
```

**Expected behavior:**

st.file_uploader works exactly the same way in a single Docker container and when deployed on Kubernetes cluster with multiple replicas.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.0.0
- Python version: 3.7.8
- continuumio/miniconda3:4.9.2 Docker image

### Additional information

The problem was reported previously in a comment https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/2803#issuecomment-948079579 , but without specific details.

title: Improve "missing ScriptRunContext" threading error

labels.name: type:enhancement
labels.description: Requests for feature enhancements or new features

labels.name: area:backend
labels.description: Related to Python backend

labels.name: area:threading/processing
labels.description: Related to threading and multiprocessing

body:
If you create a thread from your Streamlit script, and call streamlit functions from within that thread, you need to attach a `ReportContext` to it or else your `st.foo()` calls won't do anything, and you'll get a warning message that looks something like this:

“Thread ‘Thread-7’: missing ReportContext”

We should improve the error message to tell the user how to fix this! (We may just want an FAQ entry that we can link to from the error message.)

(The fix is to use `add_report_ctx` on the thread immediately after it's created:)

```python
from streamlit.ReportThread import add_report_ctx

thread = threading.Thread(target=...)
add_report_ctx(thread)
thread.start()
```

Related discussion: https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/how-to-run-a-subprocess-programs-using-thread-inside-streamlit/2440

(2022 edit: please see my comments [here](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/1326#issuecomment-1024399877) - this is an internal Streamlit API and has some major caveats. In particular, please *do not* call `st.foo` commands from other threads - at least in production code that needs to be stable.)

body:
### Problem

I'm always frustrated when I am trying to display the multiindex dataframe, but it is not readable

### Solution

`pandas` when displaying a dataframe that have multiindex skips duplicate values to make the console output a bit easier on the eyes.
```pycon
>>> import pandas as pd
>>> import numpy as np
>>>
>>> tuples = list(
...     zip(
...         *[
...             ["bar", "bar", "baz", "baz", "foo", "foo", "qux", "qux"],
...             ["one", "two", "one", "two", "one", "two", "one", "two"],
...         ]
...     )
... )
>>> index = pd.MultiIndex.from_tuples(tuples, names=["first", "second"])
>>> df = pd.DataFrame(np.random.randn(8, 2), index=index, columns=["A", "B"])
>>> df
                     A         B
first second
bar   one    -0.883183  0.480221
      two     0.861466 -0.659678
baz   one    -0.039308  0.116815
      two     0.139792  0.787177
foo   one     1.638924 -0.135970
      two     0.408906  0.394975
qux   one    -0.467613 -0.239692
      two     1.315613  0.867033
```
I think it's worth the `st.table` command to work in a similar way. Currently the table is displayed as below:
![Screenshot 2022-09-19 at 12 29 18](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/78743291/190998775-8580aecf-1a48-43a3-9640-46c464406d7d.png)

As a workaround, we can render the table to HTML via pandas, but that's not perfect.
![Screenshot 2022-09-19 at 12 30 42](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/78743291/190998928-c1307890-80f5-472b-b41e-09e957c2c3b8.png)

This is especially valuable for pivot tables.
```pycon
>>> import pandas as pd
>>> import numpy as np
>>> df = pd.DataFrame(
...     {
...         "A": ["one", "one", "two", "three"] * 3,
...         "B": ["A", "B", "C"] * 4,
...         "C": ["foo", "foo", "foo", "bar", "bar", "bar"] * 2,
...         "D": np.random.randn(12),
...         "E": np.random.randn(12),
...     }
... )
>>> pd.pivot_table(df, values="D", index=["A", "B"], columns=["C"])
C             bar       foo
A     B
one   A  0.590631  0.536188
      B  0.933343 -0.708869
      C  0.521529  0.377555
three A -0.665092       NaN
      B       NaN  1.060647
      C -1.138812       NaN
two   A       NaN  0.500034
      B  0.074022       NaN
      C       NaN  0.810322
```


### Additional context

[MultiIndex / advanced indexing](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/user_guide/advanced.html#multiindex-advanced-indexing) in pandas documentation

title: Bring your own Redis cache

labels.name: type:enhancement
labels.description: Requests for feature enhancements or new features

labels.name: feature:cache
labels.description: Related to `st.cache_data` and `st.cache_resource`

labels.name: type:possible-component
labels.description: Could be implemented as a custom component

body:
### Problem

Our micro-service hosting platform will auto-scale a service so that multiple instances are created or destroyed to adapt to varying traffic load. A user request might be routed to any one of these instances, as they are assumed to be stateless. However, our Streamlit dashboard service is not stateless due to the way session state and caches are implemented.

At the moment each instance of the service has its own Streamlit cache, which means users will often get a cache hit that’s followed immediately by a miss when their next request gets routed to another instance. We also get problems with session state not being mirrored across instances.

### Solution

Our platform provides Redis resources that are shared between instances so that to users there appears to be a single cache (rather than one per instance). What I want to do is to tell Streamlit to use this shared Redis resource as the cache, also using it to store session state.

### Additional context

We are not using Streamlit Cloud because we have our own PaaS that runs on AWS, so we want our Streamlit services to run there in order to comply with security policies for internal tools like dashboards.

body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

This issue is practically the same as this closed issue: #7354
But since it is closed (due to the user not really needing the particular use case) I have opened this new one with another simple minimum reproducible example.

### Reproducible Code Example

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-7749)

```Python
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

# using session state, works ever other input:
if "df" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.df = pd.DataFrame({"In":[0,1,2],"Out":[0,0,0]})
st.session_state.df = st.data_editor(st.session_state.df)
st.session_state.df["Out"] = st.session_state.df["In"]**2
st.write(st.session_state.df)

# # works every input but the df is not updated in data_editor:
# df = pd.DataFrame({"In":[0,1,2],"Out":[0,0,0]})
# df = st.data_editor(df)
# df["Out"] = df["In"]**2
# st.write(df)
```


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Click on a field in the in column.
2. Input a number, enter.
3. Watch for changes in the dataframes.

### Expected Behavior

I expect that each input in the data_editor to result in the rest of the code to run, before it loops back to the top and into the data_editor with new data which is displayed.
In this example I expect the "state" version to behave just like the "non-state" example, with the added functionality of the state of course.

### Current Behavior

1. I input a number(say 5) in a input field press enter.
2. This new input is replaced with the previous value instantly.
3. I input 5 in the same box again.
4. The edit_data frame now has the correct input, but not the updated input. The st.write frame is updated to reflect the correct values.

Another variant:
1. I input 5 in row 1. -> instantly replaced, nothing in st.write

title: st.dialog Does Not Close Immediately After User Action if Followed by Blocking Operation (e.g. time.sleep(15))

labels.name: type:enhancement
labels.description: Requests for feature enhancements or new features

labels.name: status:confirmed
labels.description: Bug has been confirmed by the Streamlit team

labels.name: feature:st.dialog
labels.description: Related to `st.dialog`

body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When using `st.dialog` to collect feedback from a user, if the feedback submission is followed by a blocking operation (e.g., `time.sleep(15)`), the dialog's title remains visible on the screen until the blocking operation is complete. This creates a poor user experience because the user may expect the dialog to disappear immediately after submitting their input, but the dialog remains visible until the blocking operation finishes.


### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import time
import streamlit as st

@st.dialog("Cast your vote")
def vote(item):
    st.write(f"Why is {item} your favorite?")
    reason = st.text_input("Because...")
    if st.button("Submit"):
        st.session_state.vote = {"item": item, "reason": reason}
        st.rerun()

if "vote" not in st.session_state:
    st.write("Vote for your favorite")

    if st.button("A"):
        vote("A")
    if st.button("B"):
        vote("B")
else:
    time.sleep(15)
    f"You voted for {st.session_state.vote['item']} because {st.session_state.vote['reason']}"
```


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Use the provided code below to mimic collecting user feedback using `st.dialog`.
2. After the user submits their feedback, the code simulates a blocking operation using `time.sleep(15)`.
3. Notice that the dialog's title ("Cast your vote") remains visible for the full 15 seconds while `time.sleep(15)` is running.

### Expected Behavior

The dialog should close immediately after the user submits their input, regardless of any blocking operation that follows, so that the UI responds promptly to the user's action.

### Current Behavior

The dialog remains open until the blocking operation (`time.sleep(15)`) is completed. This means the title "Cast your vote" is displayed on the screen for 15 seconds.

![2024-09-04_21-39-12 (1)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f664f9f7-24cf-4b3b-8fad-d5fdcf0dcfdb)


### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.37.1
- Python version: 3.9
- Operating System: Mac OS / Linux Ubuntu 
- Browser: Chrome 


### Additional Information

### GIF:
_Attach a GIF that shows the issue occurring._

### Additional Context:

I plan to use `st.dialog` to collect user confirmation before running a long operation. However, due to this behavior, the dialog title remains visible until the operation completes, making the user experience confusing. Ideally, the dialog should close immediately after the user interaction, regardless of subsequent operations.

title: on_change not called for first session_state value

labels.name: type:enhancement
labels.description: Requests for feature enhancements or new features

labels.name: feature:state
labels.description: Related to state management

labels.name: feature:st.session_state
labels.description: Related to session state management

body:
### Summary

Streamlit 0.84 introduces an [`on_change` callback](https://docs.streamlit.io/en/stable/session_state_api.html#use-callbacks-to-update-session-state) for some interactive widgets as part of the new Session State API. I've found that the callback is not invoked for the first value (i.e., the widget's default or initial value), only for subsequent values.  

### Steps to reproduce

Code snippet:

```python
import streamlit as st

def colour_changed():
    st.info(f"colour_changed: {st.session_state.colour}")

colour = st.selectbox("Colour", ["blue", "red", "yellow", "green"], key="colour", on_change=colour_changed)

st.info(f"selectbox returned: {colour}")
```

1. When the report is first run, the selectbox returns `blue` as the selected value, but the `colour_changed()` callback is not called.
2. When a different colour is selected, the selectbox returns the new colour and `colour_changed()` is called.
 
**Expected behavior:**

I believe the `on_change` callback should be called when a widget sets the initial/default value.

I'm finding that the lack of a callback for the initial value greatly complicates things because I can't depend on the callback to do stuff for every value of an interactive widget. I have to write special cases for the initial state.

This is further complicated by what seems like a bug initializing default session_state values for widgets like selectbox (see #3598).

**Actual behavior:**

The `on_change` callback is not called for a widget's initial/default value.

### Is this a regression?

No. The Session State API is new in Streamlit 0.84.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: Streamlit, version 0.84.2
- Python version: Python 3.8.11
- Using Conda? PipEnv? PyEnv? Pex? Just pip
- OS version: Debian buster (in a python:3.8 container)
- Browser version: Safari 14.1 on macOS Mojave 10.14.6

### Additional information

None.
